title: Compact response factory: provenance metadata and graceful rehydration
creator: Nora Patel
description: Introduce a compact, provenance-aware response factory for the Python SDK that enables lightweight typed-model hydration (dataclasses and optional pydantic fallbacks), preserves streaming provenance metadata across retries/checkpoints, and provides ergonomic helpers for partial/gradual rehydration during streaming and retry scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: A1: SDK exposes ResponseFactory.compact_hydrate(payload, model=...) which attaches provenance headers and returns either a dataclass instance or a controlled ValidationError wrapper
A2: Streaming iterator API preserves provenance tokens (request_id, model_version, kv_prefix_offsets) and reinjects them on retry so downstream consumers can correlate partial fragments
A3: Backcompat shim covers legacy JSON envelopes with a migration map; no consumer-level breakages in existing integration tests
A4: Unit tests cover partial hydration (missing fields), idempotent resume after retry, and performance benchmark showing <5% overhead for provenance encoding in common paths
A5: Docs and two short examples (sync and async streaming) added to SDK docs and quickstart
technical_notes: Design favors dataclass-first approach: lightweight generated dataclasses for 80% of use cases, optional pydantic model for strict validation on demand
Provenance metadata is a small protobuf-ish header (base64 compact JSON) attached to first stream chunk and mirrored on retry headers (X-RW-Provenance)
Hydration should be tolerant: missing optional fields are allowed; required fields produce RecoverableValidationError that contains raw_fragment and hydration_stack for inspection

Retry flow: on transient transport failure the iterator yields a checkpoint token; caller can call resume(checkpoint) which requests remaining tokens including provenance to perform deterministic rehydration
Performance: avoid deep copies during streaming—hydrate in-place as bytes arrive up to a configurable buffering threshold (default 512 bytes)
implementation_plan: 1) Design doc + API proposal (link in related_links) and small design review - owner: Nora
2) Implement ResponseFactory.compact_hydrate and RecoverableValidationError in sdk-python/core - owner: Diego
3) Add streaming provenance header implementation in runtime-client and wire through streaming iterator - owner: runtime team collaborator
4) Create backcompat shim mapping for legacy JSON envelopes and tests using fixtures from old API responses
5) Add unit/integration tests: hydration, resume-after-retry, end-to-end streaming example
6) Add docs and code snippets for both sync and async streaming, and publish SDK changelog entry
7) Release in sdk-python-2.4 canary, monitor telemetry for error spikes and latency changes
